pages.text: Every morning on Market Street, ten-year-old Yao and nine-year-old Akosua heard the same complaints. The bread seller sighed at plastic water sachets blowing past her stall. The trotro driver frowned at the overflowing skip container by the junction. The tailor shook his head at the roadside gutter choked with silt and bottles. Yet everyone ended with the exact same sentence: ‘Why hasn’t Somebody fixed this yet?’
sentences: Every morning on Market Street, ten-year-old Yao and nine-year-old Akosua heard the same complaints.
The bread seller sighed at plastic water sachets blowing past her stall.
The trotro driver frowned at the overflowing skip container by the junction.
The tailor shook his head at the roadside gutter choked with silt and bottles.
Yet everyone ended with the exact same sentence: ‘Why hasn’t Somebody fixed this yet?’
pages.alt: On a busy Ghanaian street, shopkeepers and drivers shrug at windblown plastic sachets and an overflowing bin while Yao and Akosua walk to school.

pages.text: At school, Akosua raised her hand in Mr Mensah’s class. ‘Sir, everyone in town is waiting for a person named Somebody! Can our class go and dig out the deep roadside gutter ourselves after school?’ Mr Mensah smiled warmly at her spirit, then raised his hand in a firm safety stop.
sentences: At school, Akosua raised her hand in Mr Mensah’s class.

pages.alt: In the Primary 4 classroom, Akosua raises her hand eagerly while Mr Mensah makes a calm safety stop gesture.

pages.text: ‘Your care for our town is wonderful, Akosua,’ said Mr Mensah, ‘but children must NEVER enter deep roadside gutters, touch sharp metal or broken glass, or handle medical or hazardous waste! Clearing heavy public drains and hauling municipal skips is the job of trained adult sanitation workers with boots, shovels and trucks. However, there are two powerful, safe things we CAN do!’
sentences: ‘Your care for our town is wonderful, Akosua,’ said Mr Mensah, ‘but children must NEVER enter deep roadside gutters, touch sharp metal or broken glass, or handle medical or hazardous waste!
Clearing heavy public drains and hauling municipal skips is the job of trained adult sanitation workers with boots, shovels and trucks.
However, there are two powerful, safe things we CAN do!’
pages.alt: Mr Mensah points to a safety chart showing adult sanitation workers with protective boots and trucks vs safe school recycling tasks.

pages.text: ‘First,’ explained Mr Mensah, ‘we stop adding to the problem by sorting clean, dry recyclables right here in our school compound and homes. Second, we gather clear evidence and invite our local government representative, the Assembly Member, and our parents to do their part!’ That afternoon, with reusable gloves and Mr Mensah’s supervision, the class set up three painted barrels in the schoolyard: Green for clean plastic, Blue for paper and card, and Brown for fruit peels to make garden compost.
sentences: ‘First,’ explained Mr Mensah, ‘we stop adding to the problem by sorting clean, dry recyclables right here in our school compound and homes.

Second, we gather clear evidence and invite our local government representative, the Assembly Member, and our parents to do their part!’ That afternoon, with reusable gloves and Mr Mensah’s supervision, the class set up three painted barrels in the schoolyard: Green for clean plastic, Blue for paper and card, and Brown for fruit peels to make garden compost.
pages.alt: Under Mr Mensah’s supervision in the schoolyard, Yao and Akosua place clean plastic bottles and paper into green, blue and brown sorting barrels.

pages.text: At the end of the week, a licensed plastic-recycling van visited the school gate to weigh their clean, dry collection. The class had collected forty kilograms of clean plastic bottles and sachets plus twenty kilograms of old paper and cardboard, sixty kilograms of waste kept out of the gutters! Even better, the recycler paid the school two cedis per kilogram of plastic, earning eighty cedis for new library storybooks!

pages.alt: At the school gate, a recycling collector weighs the sacks of clean plastic bottles on a scale while Yao, Akosua and Mr Mensah celebrate.

pages.text: Next came Step Two: civic accountability! Walking safely along the dry pavement with Mr Mensah and two parents, Yao and Akosua conducted a Neighbourhood Sanitation Audit from a safe distance. Using a map and tally sheet, they recorded three places where public waste bins were missing and two junctions where the large municipal skip had not been emptied on schedule.

pages.alt: Walking safely on the pavement with Mr Mensah and two parents, Yao and Akosua mark missing bin locations on a clipboard map.

pages.text: With Mr Mensah’s help, the pupils and the Parent-Teacher Association wrote a polite, factual letter to Honourable Tetteh, the Assembly Member for their electoral area, attaching their map and sixty signatures from shopkeepers and parents. On Wednesday afternoon, Honourable Tetteh and an officer from the District Assembly Environmental Health Department arrived at the school hall to meet the community.
sentences: With Mr Mensah’s help, the pupils and the Parent-Teacher Association wrote a polite, factual letter to Honourable Tetteh, the Assembly Member for their electoral area, attaching their map and sixty signatures from shopkeepers and parents.

pages.alt: In the school hall, Yao and Akosua present their colourful sanitation map to Honourable Tetteh, the environmental health officer and parents.

pages.text: Honourable Tetteh studied the map and nodded seriously. ‘Thank you for bringing clear facts instead of just grumbling on the street,’ he said. ‘Our District Assembly collects market tolls and property rates to fund sanitation. I will make sure the Waste Management Department sets a fixed Tuesday and Friday truck schedule for the junction skip and installs four new lidded street bins this month!’
sentences: Honourable Tetteh studied the map and nodded seriously.

I will make sure the Waste Management Department sets a fixed Tuesday and Friday truck schedule for the junction skip and installs four new lidded street bins this month!’
pages.alt: Honourable Tetteh signs the new waste-collection schedule while the environmental health officer points to four new lidded bin locations on the map.

pages.text: Then the environmental health officer turned to the shopkeepers, drivers and parents in the hall. ‘When the Assembly truck empties the skip and our adult crew clears the heavy drains on Saturday,’ she said, ‘every adult resident and trader must also keep a covered bin at their stall, stop sweeping plastic into the gutter, and report missed pickups promptly. Clean towns need both responsible citizens and working public services!’

Clean towns need both responsible citizens and working public services!’
pages.alt: Adult municipal sanitation workers in boots and safety vests clear the roadside drain with long shovels while shopkeepers place covered bins beside their stalls.

pages.text: A month later, when the first heavy rains fell, rainwater flowed smoothly through the clear street drains without flooding a single shop! Market Street had new lidded bins, the skip truck arrived every Tuesday and Friday, and four more schools copied Primary 4’s recycling barrels. Yao and Akosua grinned at each other. Nobody was waiting for "Somebody" anymore, because citizens and local government were finally working together!

activities.question: Why did Mr Mensah tell the pupils they must NEVER enter deep roadside gutters or touch sharp/hazardous waste?
options: It is unsafe for children; heavy drains require trained adult crews
Mr Mensah wanted the gutters to stay blocked forever
Plastic bottles dissolve by themselves in two minutes
activities.explanation: Children’s safety comes first: heavy drains and hazardous waste require trained adult sanitation crews with protective equipment.

activities.definition: Decayed plant and fruit peels that turn into rich natural fertilizer for garden soil
distractors: Plastic water sachets thrown into a roadside gutter
A metal truck used by the District Assembly

activities.question: When the school collected 40 kg of clean plastic and 20 kg of paper, what was the total weight and the 2-cedi/kg plastic earnings?
options: 60 kg recycled in total, earning 80 cedis for library books
20 kg recycled in total, earning 10 cedis
100 kg recycled in total, earning 500 cedis
activities.explanation: 40 kg + 20 kg = 60 kg total; 40 kg of plastic × 2 cedis per kg = 80 cedis.

activities.question: How did the town solve the sanitation problem sustainably?
options: Citizens sorted waste while the Assembly sent bins, trucks and crews
Primary 4 pupils replaced the municipal waste department permanently
Everyone kept waiting for a stranger named Somebody
activities.explanation: Lasting sanitation requires both everyday citizen responsibility and accountable municipal public services.

activities.prompt: Put the steps of Primary 4’s safe citizenship project in order.
items: Sort clean plastic, paper and compost safely inside the schoolyard.
Map missing street bins from the pavement and petition the Assembly.
Pair adult drain crews and skip trucks with clean community habits.

activities.prompt: How did moving from complaining ("Why hasn’t Somebody fixed this?") to safe teamwork change how everyone felt about their town?

Systems and practices that keep a community clean and protect public health through safe waste and drain management

Able to be washed and used again many times
